cards.front: Recall a key point about The Conflict of the Orders
cards.back: The Conflict of the Orders (494-287 BC) was the struggle between patricians and plebeians for political equality

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Conflict of the Orders
cards.back: The First Secession (494 BC): plebeians withdrew to the Sacred Mount, forcing the patricians to create the tribunes of the plebs

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Conflict of the Orders
cards.back: The Twelve Tables (451-450 BC): Rome's first written law code, created because plebeians were being judged by unwritten patrician customs

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Conflict of the Orders
cards.back: The Licinian-Sextian Laws (367 BC) required one consul to be a plebeian; the office was opened to plebeians

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Conflict of the Orders
cards.back: The Hortensian Law (287 BC) made plebiscites (laws passed by the plebeian assembly) binding on all citizens, effectively ending the Conflict

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Conflict of the Orders
cards.back: Key tactics: secession (plebeians refusing to serve in the army or work), tribunician veto, and threat of mass action
